boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named campus spaces for focused work, collaboration, creative projects, reflection, academic support, and time outdoors.

cards.entity_name: Sterling C. Evans Library Quiet Floors
cards.title: Sterling C. Evans Library Quiet Floors
cards.subtitle: Evans Library, 3rd and 5th floors
cards.notes: Choose an open quiet floor for focused coursework, and reserve an individual room when one is available for the study session you need.
cards.short_summary: Quiet floors and individual rooms give solo work a defined campus setting.
cards.evidence_claim: Evans Library has quiet open-study space on its third and fifth floors, plus individual study rooms.
cards.access_notes: Quiet-space rules prohibit talking, calls, video chat, and speakers; some rooms are reservable while others are first-come.

cards.title: West Campus Library
cards.subtitle: 214 Olsen Blvd
cards.notes: Use the third-floor quiet area when you need independent focus, or choose a group room and library services for a course-related work session.
cards.short_summary: A west-side library with quiet study, group rooms, course reserves, computers, and equipment checkout.
cards.evidence_claim: West Campus Library offers group study rooms, an individual quiet-study floor, computers, course reserves, printing, and Tech Bar equipment checkout.
cards.source_title: About West Campus Library | University Libraries
cards.access_notes: The quiet-study area is on the third floor; group study rooms are intended for collaborative academic activity.

cards.title: Kelsey Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Cushing Memorial Library & Archives, 400 Spence St.
cards.notes: Plan a daytime quiet-work visit, or request archival material in advance through Aeon and wait for Cushing staff to confirm the appointment.
cards.short_summary: A 38-seat archival reading room that also permits quiet study.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kelsey Reading Room is available for using Cushing collection materials and as a quiet study space; it has 38 seats and two OAL computers.
cards.source_title: Planning Your Visit | Cushing Memorial Library & Archives
cards.access_notes: Listed standard hours are Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–4:30 p.m.; archival-material users need an Aeon account and a confirmed appointment.

cards.title: The Studio
cards.subtitle: Evans Annex, sixth floor, Room 3.653
cards.notes: Reserve a space for a course media project, then use the One Button Studio, Whisper Rooms, or editing bays with the equipment listed by the library.
cards.short_summary: A library multimedia workspace for recording, editing, and production support.
cards.evidence_claim: The Studio provides multimedia tools and assistance, including a One Button Studio, Whisper Rooms, and editing bays.
cards.access_notes: Located in Evans Annex Room 3.653; Studio spaces can be reserved through the library’s reservation link.

cards.title: The Maker Zone
cards.subtitle: Texas A&M University Libraries
cards.notes: Bring a valid Aggie ID, check the open-studio or workshop schedule, and ask staff before using unfamiliar machines or materials.
cards.short_summary: An experiential learning space for campus-affiliated makers, with workshops and open-studio time.
cards.evidence_claim: The Maker Zone is an experiential learning space for current Texas A&M students, faculty, and staff, with workshops and open studio times.
cards.access_notes: A valid Aggie ID is required; follow staff direction and equipment safety policies while using the space.

cards.title: Math Learning Center
cards.subtitle: Evans Library, second floor
cards.notes: Use the center’s tutoring, study sessions, workshops, or weekly reviews to work through quantitative course material with academic support.
cards.short_summary: A campus academic unit supporting math, statistics, and quantitative-reasoning courses.
cards.evidence_claim: The Math Learning Center supports Texas A&M students in high-enrollment mathematics, statistics, and quantitative-reasoning courses through tutoring, study sessions, workshops, and weekly reviews.
cards.access_notes: The manual lists a location on the second floor of Evans Library; check the Math Learning Center for current support schedules.

cards.title: University Writing Center
cards.subtitle: Evans Library, second floor
cards.notes: Bring a draft or speaking plan to a one-to-one or group consultation, and use the center’s workshops or writing-group options to keep a project moving.
cards.short_summary: Consultation and workshop support for writing and public speaking across disciplines.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Writing Center provides graduate and undergraduate students one-to-one and group consultations, online or face-to-face, for writing and public speaking.
cards.access_notes: The manual lists the center on Evans Library’s second floor; consult the center’s site for appointments and current offerings.

cards.title: Memorial Student Center
cards.subtitle: 275 Joe Routt Blvd
cards.notes: Use the building as a practical meet-up point before a campus program, then check its current events, offices, dining, vendors, and reservable spaces.
cards.short_summary: A campus center with event space, offices, vendors, dining, and entertainment.
cards.evidence_claim: The Memorial Student Center hosts vendors and services, dining and entertainment, offices, and reservable event spaces.
cards.source_title: Memorial Student Center | University Center & Special Events
cards.access_notes: The university lists seasonal building hours and a reservation process; confirm details before planning an event or visit.

cards.title: Aggie Park
cards.subtitle: Campus park near the Memorial Student Center
cards.notes: Set up a low-key outdoor study break or meet friends by the lawns and activity areas, while keeping reserved event and tailgating areas clear.
cards.short_summary: A 20-acre campus park with outdoor space for study, relaxation, recreation, and entertainment.
cards.evidence_claim: Aggie Park contains more than 20 acres of outdoor space for study, relaxation, entertainment, and recreation for students, staff, faculty, and visitors.
cards.source_title: Aggie Park | University Center & Special Events
cards.access_notes: The park is listed as open 24/7; tailgating spaces require reservations, including free university-managed options.

cards.title: All Faiths Chapel
cards.subtitle: Texas A&M University campus
cards.notes: Use this shared setting for a quiet moment of reflection or to arrange an eligible faith-related gathering through the university reservation process.
cards.short_summary: A campus chapel serving all denominations and creeds, with meditation rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: All Faiths Chapel serves all denominations and creeds and includes chapel and meditation-room spaces.
cards.source_title: All Faiths Chapel | University Center & Special Events
cards.access_notes: The university lists the chapel as open 24/7; reservations are required for reserved venue use.
